_comment: temper-rust-router-core's expected-failure manifest, the sibling of
wasm_expected_failures.json (temper-drc-rs), wasm_expected_failures_geometry.json and
wasm_expected_failures_thermal.json. Same contract, same reasoning -- see
wasm_expected_failures.json's _comment for why divergences are LISTED and executed
rather than deleted or cfg'd out.
It is a separate file rather than more entries in a shared one because
run_wasm_tests.mjs exits non-zero on an ORPHAN EXCLUSION: a manifest entry naming no
registered test. Point the runner at this one with
`--expected-failures tools/wasm/wasm_expected_failures_router_core.json` when the
module carries temper-rust-router-core alone (`make wasm-router-core-test` does).
THIS CRATE CURRENTLY HAS NO NATIVE-VS-WASM32 DIVERGENCES. `expected_failures` is
empty, and that is a measurement, not an oversight.
Measured 2026-08-11 against 111 registered tests: 111 pass, 0 expected-fail, 0 other.
Native, for contrast: `cargo test --manifest-path
packages/temper-rust-router-core/Cargo.toml` passes 154/155 (1 ignored) on
x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu. wasm32 now agrees with the host on every registered test.
History. Until #946 this file listed 23 entries, all ONE class (`no-clock`) and ONE
root cause: combinator::rewrite::rewrite() built a RewriteTrace whose `start:
Instant::now()` was evaluated unconditionally -- beside, not behind, the
TEMPER_REWRITE_TRACE `enabled` flag -- and its trace call sites passed eagerly
formatted `&str`s, so ~10 further Instant::now()/elapsed() readings happened before
log() could consult `enabled`. wasm32-unknown-unknown's std has no clock:
Instant::now() panics with 'time not implemented on this platform'
(library/std/src/sys/time/unsupported.rs:13). The panic was in PRODUCTION code, so
the honest reading was 'combinator::rewrite does not run on wasm32', not '23 flaky
tests'. #946 made the timestamp an Option acquired only when tracing is on and gave
log() a closure so its arguments are not evaluated on the disabled path; all 23
entries turned into passes and were deleted here in the same PR. Same defect shape,
same fix, and same reconciliation as temper-geometry's #941/#942.
The gate is bidirectional, which is what keeps this emptiness honest in both
directions: a listed test that starts passing is reported as an UNEXPECTED PASS and
exits non-zero (that is how the 23 above were identified -- by running the module,
not by reading a diff), and a test that starts failing with nothing listed here is a
plain FAIL. An empty manifest therefore means every registered test really runs on
wasm32, and any new divergence has to be added deliberately.
